clue.text: Hesitation about company truly getting back to normal

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the hesitation word is read backwards

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
truly means very, as in 'yours very sincerely'

explanation.surface: A firm's honest hesitancy is part of its return to business as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but is the reversal signal on the hesitation sound; 'truly' gives its everyday synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovery is the process of returning to a healthy or settled state, a synonym for the gerund phrase.

clue.text: Directions ready for putting outside city area

indicators.note: the ripe word is put outside the city letters, which go within it

parts.note: ripe means ready, as fruit is
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: Instructions primed for carrying out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postcode district of the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is a set of instructions for cooking a dish.

clue.text: Conservative spouse a bit on the fat side

definitions.text: a bit on the fat side

parts.note: hubby is an informal word for husband

explanation.surface: A Tory's husband is a little overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Chubby means plump, slightly overweight.

clue.text: One composer or another getting half cut

indicators.note: half cut means half the letters of the other composer's name are chopped off

parts.note: another composer, here Monteverdi, the Italian Renaissance composer

explanation.surface: Two composers, one of them slightly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' (British slang for tipsy) cuts the first half, MONTE, from MONTEVERDI.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi was an Italian opera composer, writer of Aida and La Traviata.

clue.text: Greek character, doctor, joins American mathematical figure

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
US for the United States

explanation.surface: A Greek, a medic and an American team up over geometry.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is a parallelogram with four equal sides, a shape in geometry.

clue.text: Food ugly woman served to soldiers

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old woman
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: An unattractive woman dishes up a meal to the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: HAGGIS is a Scottish dish of offal, oatmeal and spices cooked in a sheep's stomach; 'served to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis is a traditional Scottish dish, so an example of food.

clue.text: Bitter stuff upsetting Aaron's gut

indicators.note: upsetting suggests the letters of Aaron's gut are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: the letters of Aaron's, possessive S included

explanation.surface: A sour drink gives someone an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' rearranges AARONS and GUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Angostura is aromatic bitters used to flavour drinks.

clue.text: Man turned up on time with bad-mannered woman

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Reg is a man's name, short for Reginald
rude means impolite

explanation.surface: A man arrives punctually with an impolite female companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like 'arrived' but reverses REG to GER; 'on' places it above T in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Gertrude is a female name, so stands for a woman.

clue.text: Tree sounding less healthy again

indicators.note: sounding means the words for less healthy and again are said out loud

parts.note: sicker means more ill; more means once again, additionally

explanation.surface: Someone sounds as though they are getting worse once more.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, SICKER MORE runs together as a match for the tree's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The sycamore is a large maple tree common in Britain.

clue.text: Garden disease? Hit the source

parts.note: to club is to hit with a heavy stick
the root of something is its origin or source

explanation.surface: A gardener blames a plant disease and wants to strike at its origin.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubroot is a fungal-type infection of cabbages and other brassicas, a common garden disease.

clue.text: A plant left out gets fungus

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is taken away from the plant name

parts.note: garlic is a plant of the onion family

explanation.surface: A neglected plant left outside goes mouldy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' looks like a plant neglected outside, but 'out' is the deletion signal and 'left' its letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An agaric is a mushroom with gills, a kind of fungus.

clue.text: Tot will need doctor in the morning

parts.note: a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A small child must see the GP first thing tomorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a toddler but is a small measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small measure of whisky or spirits, as is a dram.

clue.text: Pole to open place in the hostelry

indicators.note: to here means attached onto, so the pole word joins the end of the open word

parts.note: public means open to all
a bar is a rod or pole

explanation.surface: Someone is told to use a pole to open something at the inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' is not a Polish person but a rod, BAR. A PUBLIC BAR is the plainer room of a British pub, as against the lounge or saloon.
explanation.definitionFit: The public bar is one of the rooms in a pub, an inn or hostelry.

clue.text: Kent's alcoholic drink? Watery stuff!

parts.note: Kent is a county in the South East of England, abbreviated SE
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a weak drink is a Kent speciality.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England, so SE stands for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Serum is the thin watery fluid left when blood clots, so watery stuff.

clue.text: People being paid writing junk English!

indicators.note: junk as a verb means throw away, so the letter for English is discarded

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language

explanation.surface: Paid writers are accused of churning out rubbish English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'junk' looks like an insult to the writing but tells you to drop E (English) from PROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pros are professionals, those who earn money for what they do.

clue.text: See the man who married Jane Eyre

definitions.meaning: a bishop's seat or diocese, here a cathedral city in Kent

definitions.text: the man who married Jane Eyre
definitions.meaning: Edward Fairfax ___, the hero of Charlotte Bronte's novel

explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a bishop's diocese; this one is a cathedral city in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: The diocese of a bishop based in a Kent cathedral city shares its name with the brooding hero of Charlotte Bronte's novel.

clue.text: Grumble with mum falling short

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
under means below the required amount

explanation.surface: Someone moans about a mother who doesn't measure up.
explanation.definitionFit: To maunder is to mutter or complain in a rambling way.

clue.text: Reveller in merry-go-round finally changing

indicators.note: finally changing says the last letter of the fairground ride is swapped for another

parts.note: a carousel is a merry-go-round

explanation.surface: Someone enjoying a fairground ride undergoes a change at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally changing' swaps the last letter of CAROUSEL, L, for R.
explanation.definitionFit: A carouser is someone who drinks and makes merry noisily.

clue.text: One lying down between steps

parts.note: suggests a person resting on the staircase, but means a metal rod holding a carpet in the angle of each stair

explanation.definitionFit: A stair rod lies along the base of each riser, holding the carpet runner flat in place.

clue.text: It could be a thing you read in the paper

definitions.meaning: the word 'a' is an indefinite ... in grammar

definitions.text: thing you read in the paper

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads 'a' as the word itself: 'a' is the indefinite article.
explanation.definitionFit: Both grammar's 'a' and 'the' and a newspaper report are called by this word: one a part of speech, one a written piece.

clue.text: Welshman upsetting part of the church

indicators.note: upsetting in a down entry means turning the church word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: A man from Wales is causing trouble in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Evan is a typically Welsh male name, so it stands for a man from Wales.

clue.text: One of four children in the college square?

definitions.meaning: short for quadruplet, one of four born at a birth
short for quadrangle, a courtyard in a college

explanation.definitionFit: The word is short both for quadruplet, one of a set of four siblings, and for quadrangle, a courtyard.

clue.text: Queen wants an outhouse demolished

parts.note: an gives the letter A
a shed is an outbuilding

explanation.surface: Her Majesty wants an outbuilding pulled down.
explanation.definitionFit: To quash is to crush or put down, so quashed fits demolished in the sense of overthrown.

clue.text: Hairy model enthralling the Spanish

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the model word wraps around the article

parts.note: to pose is to model for an artist
intended as a foreign word for the; IL is in fact the Italian article

explanation.surface: A furry model has Spanish admirers spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish for 'the' is EL; only the Italian IL gives the answer, so 'Spanish' is a slip for Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilose is a botanical and zoological term for covered with soft hairs.

clue.text: Musical group arranged around piano out of this world

indicators.note: around says the arranged word is placed on either side of the letter for piano

parts.note: set means arranged, as in set out
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
ET is the extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: A band plays a rearranged piece round the piano that is simply sublime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' looks like an anagram signal but gives SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A septet is a group of seven musicians.

clue.text: Think of female leaving, then waste away

indicators.note: leaving says the letter for female goes out of the word of

parts.note: to pine is to waste away from grief

explanation.surface: A woman departs and someone is left to languish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes F (female) out of OF, leaving O.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to hold or state an opinion, to think.

clue.text: A mother pig in the water

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
swine is another word for pig

explanation.surface: A sow wallowing in a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word here, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's wine is a humorous old name for water, the only drink in Eden.

clue.text: Opening Thomas found in south Africa

indicators.note: found in says the short name for Thomas sits inside the two compass and continent letters

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for Africa
Tom is short for Thomas

explanation.surface: A man named Thomas turns up in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south Africa' looks like the country but is two abbreviations, S and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoma is a pore or mouth-like opening, in a leaf or made surgically.

clue.text: In forest rat attacks layers

indicators.note: In tells you the letters sit inside the words forest rat attacks

explanation.surface: A rodent in the woods goes on the offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are beds or levels of rock, layers.

clue.text: Drive away illegal ticket seller in decisive action

parts.note: to shoo is to drive away with a wave
a tout sells tickets unofficially at inflated prices

explanation.surface: Chasing off a ticket tout counts as firm intervention.
explanation.walkthrough: A tout in Britain is a scalper.
explanation.definitionFit: A shootout is a final confrontation or a penalty contest that settles a result.

clue.text: Jumpers possibly ruined by driers

indicators.note: ruined suggests the letters of the word driers are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Woollen sweaters spoiled by tumble driers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumpers' (British for sweaters) suggests knitwear spoilt in a drier, but means show jumpers, the people on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders in showjumping are jumpers, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: A sort of radio presenter with a bit of money next door

parts.note: a DJ or disc jockey is a kind of radio presenter
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: A disc jockey with a little cash lives nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjacent means neighbouring, lying beside something.
